# Spiritual Translation: On the Purification of the Mind through the Descent and Removal of Three Forms of Evil

---

**¶1:** When the Divine allowed these three containing forms of evil to descend from the interiors — those of corrupted falsity, of spiritual blindness, and of self-love — did the Divine perhaps cast them directly into the hells at the boundary of the interior mind? Or did the Divine first bring them into conscious awareness within the natural mind, and only then sweep them out and confine them in their appointed places?

**¶2:** When the Divine was about to remove these three containing forms of evil, it poured all three into the natural mind, one by one at the ordained time and stage of development. It allowed them to descend and settle into conscious awareness.

**¶3:** Then the Divine drew them out from the natural mind by means of three exterior truths — those of rational understanding, of genuine truth, and of purified love — which clothed the Divine presence itself. The Divine caused them to flow into the three confined regions of hell [GAP-1] which had been established during the formation of the spiritual world [GAP-2] they [GAP-3] yet something remained behind within the natural mind from these three forms of evil, so that their trace and character can be found displayed throughout the whole order of the mind.

**¶4:** The element that remains from corrupted falsity is the bitterness and corrosiveness of the pervasive sensory falsity that encompasses all the states of the mind — the acrid quality of the outermost knowledge of appearances through which everything interior is distorted.

**¶5:** And the remnant left behind from spiritual blindness is that obstinate elevation of self-intelligence that persists near the very source of illumination. For when Divine wisdom shines into the mind, no light of truth is visible in that state, because the falsity from evil that pours forth from self-intelligence manifests above it and obscures it.

**¶6:** And the remnant that remains from self-love, within the natural mind, comprises all the elevations of pride and isolated states of self-will from which exhalations of evil desire rise up and become manifest. For these are remnants of the great containing form of infernal love, the vestige that was conjoined with the concupiscence ascending from the natural mind — together with the states of pride and self-exaltation [GAP-4] states where no good works spring forth from any perception [GAP-5] greater than that state from the limb and [GAP-6] perceptions shall not bear forth good works in that condition.

**¶7:** Concerning the containing forms of evil that encompass the whole mind, and why they were not removed directly from the interiors into the hells prepared for them at once, but were first poured into the natural mind, and only afterward swept from the natural mind and cast down into their confined places.

**¶8:** When the Divine allowed these containing forms to descend from the interiors upon the natural mind, it poured them forth for this reason: so that also the corrupted falsity, the spiritual blindness, and the self-love already existing within the lower natural states would be attracted and drawn upward toward that which had descended from the interiors, and the natural states themselves would be purified and cleansed. For this purpose the Divine brought these containing forms into conscious awareness — of corrupted falsity, of spiritual blindness, and of self-love — so that the corrupted falsity, the spiritual blindness, and the self-love already embedded in the natural states would be drawn toward that which had descended from within.

**¶9:** First of all, the Divine removed the corrupted falsity — the waste and the poison of the ruling evils that dominated the interiors. The Divine cleansed the interior states of the [GAP-7: corrupted falsity]; it poured down the dark falsities. [GAP-8: Just as the] falsities descended from the interior mind into the natural mind, so also the falsities lodged below in the natural states were attracted and rose from below toward the falsities that had come from the interiors into conscious awareness. The falsities [GAP-9: were] purified of the dark poison of evil within them. Then the Divine swept them outward and made of them a great containing boundary — a wall of outermost sensory knowledge that encompasses the entire mind, and upon which doctrinal systems may navigate.

**¶10:** After the corrupted falsity, the Divine removed the spiritual blindness. It purified the interior states and dried from them the falsity from evil with which they were weighed down. It brought this blindness into the natural mind. Just as it had purified the interior states, so also it purified the natural states. The falsity from evil residing in the natural states was drawn upward toward the falsity from evil that had been discharged from the interiors. Both were swept out together and shut within that [GAP-10] region of spiritual blindness [GAP-11] the corrupted falsity.

**¶11:** And the Divine brought the self-love down from the interior states into the natural mind, [GAP-12: and at] that time again the self-love that had been confined [GAP-13: in] the natural states below was attracted and rose toward its own kind. Evil desire was added to evil desire. Afterward, the Divine swept it out and cast it into the outermost hell, which [GAP-14: had been constructed for] them beyond the whole order of the mind.

**¶12:** In the same way that the Divine purified the interior states above to become a place through which truths of illumination could journey [GAP-15] so also the Divine purified the natural states below and swept from them the self-love, the spiritual blindness, and the corrupted falsity [GAP-16]. The Divine has purified them for the ascent of the three living powers — those of rational understanding, genuine truth, and purified love — which ascend before the Guardian of the threshold and traverse all the natural states from lowest to highest.

---

### Translator's Note on the Overarching Process

The entire chapter describes what Swedenborg calls *vastation* and *purification* in regeneration. The central teaching — that evils cannot be cast directly from the interiors into the hells but must first be brought into conscious awareness in the natural mind — corresponds precisely to the doctrine that no evil can be removed unless it is first seen, acknowledged, and resisted in the external man. The descent of like toward like (evil drawing out evil of its kind) reflects the law that latent hereditary evils are activated and made manifest through temptation, so that they may be identified, separated, and removed. The three stages — corrupted falsity first, then spiritual blindness, then self-love last — follow the Swedenborgian order of reformation: falsities of the understanding are addressed before the deeper evils of the will, and self-love, being the deepest root, is removed last and cast into the outermost hell.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: When the Father of Life discharged these three vessels from above, they of water and of darkness and of fire, did he perhaps discharge them to their pits at the edge of the firmament? Or did he discharge them first to this earth, and then he swept them from the earth and threw them to their places?

when the Father of Life was about to discharge these three vessels he poured the three upon this earth, one by one at its (appointed) hour and season. He discharged them and cast them down to the earth.

Then he bailed and scooped them from this earth in these three garments, they of wind and of water and of fire, which swathed his body. He poured and made them flow into the three pits [at the edge of the firmament]hich he had [es]tablished during the construc[tio]n of the worlds [And when] they [were swept away, yet] something remained behind on the face of the earth from these three vessels, so that you can find their mark and type displayed in the universe.
The element that is left in water is the pungency and the salinity of this salty inner sea that surrounds the worlds.

And the remnant that is left from the darkness is this black mountain that exists in the surroundings of the sunrise. For when the sun would shine over the world no sunlight is visible there, because the darkness that gushes from it manifests above it.

And the remnant that remains behind from the fire, upon the earth, are all the mountains and islands from where fumes of fire gush up and are visible. For these things are the remnant of the great vessel, the vestige that was conjoined with this fire that comes up from the earth; together with the mountains and hills [and the] places where no fruit sprouts on the trees [for the fire is] greater than that place from the limb and [ ... / ... ] the trees shall not bear fruit in that place.

about the vessels that surround the universe, and why they were not discharged from above into the ditches prepared for them (straightaway); but were firstly poured upon the earth, and afterwards were swept from the earth and cast down into their pits?

When the Father of Life discharged these vessels from above upon the earth, he poured them out for this reason: so that also the water and the darkness and the fire that exist in these three earths would be drawn and ascend towards they that had come down from above, and the earths would be purified and cleansed. Due to this he poured these vessels down to the earth, of water and of darkness and of fire, so that also the water and darkness and fire that exist in the earths would be drawn up towards they that had descended from above.

Now, first of all, he discharged the water, the waste, the poison of the rulers who are above. He cleansed the firmaments of the [water that weighed them down] he poured down the dark waters. [Just as the] waters fell from heaven to earth, so also the waters below in the earths were drawn and came up from below towards the waters that had come from above to the earths. The waters [were] purified of the dark poison that exists in them. Then he swept them outside and made them a great vessel and a wall of sea that surrounds the universe, and on which the ships sail.

After the water, he discharged the darkness. He purified the firmaments and dried from them the darkness with which they are weighed down. He discharged it down to the earth. Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths. The darkness that is in the earths was drawn up towards the darkness that had been discharged from above. He swept them both out and shut them in that [pit] of darkness [ ... / ... ] the water.

And he discharged the fire from heaven to earth, [and at] that time again the fire that was shut [in] the earth below was drawn and came up towards its kind. Fire was added to fire. Afterwards, he swept it out and cast it into the outer underworld, which [he had constructed for] them outside the universe.

In the same way that he purified the firmaments above as a place for the light-givers to journey [ ... / ... ] so also he purified the earths below and swept from them the fire and the darkness and the water [and cast them out] He has purified them for the ascent of these three powers, they of the wind and the water and the fire, which ascend before the Porter and traverse the earths.

fills.explanation: This echoes the identical phrase from ¶1 ("their pits at the edge of the firmament"), which is the text's established locational descriptor for the three pits; the Kephalaia register commonly repeats such fixed phrases, and the spiritual reading places these pits at the boundary of the interior mind, corresponding to the edge of the firmament.

This introduces a temporal-concessive clause connecting the casting of vessels into the pits with the observation that remnants remained; "And when" is a natural narrative connector in Kephalaia style leading into "they were swept away, yet something remained."

The spiritual reading shows "yet" immediately after this gap's position, indicating a concessive transition; "swept away" uses the chapter's primary verb for removal (¶1, ¶7, ¶9–12), and "yet" introduces the exception that remnants remained on earth.

This connects two items in the list of fire-remnant effects: "mountains and hills" and "places where no fruit sprouts on the trees"; the simple connector "and the" follows the Kephalaia's typical list-construction pattern.

The spiritual reading indicates the intensity of self-love (fire) prevents good works (fruit) from emerging; "for the fire is" provides the causal explanation for barrenness and sets up the comparative "greater," paralleling ¶6's descriptions of volcanic fumes overwhelming vegetation.

This directly parallels ¶10's structure where the firmaments are cleansed of "the darkness with which they are weighed down"; the same participial description applies to water, expressing the corrupted falsity that burdened the interior states.

Confirming the editor's reading: this establishes the "Just as X, so also Y" parallel structure used identically in ¶10 ("Just as he had purified the firmaments, so also he purified the earths"), which is the chapter's consistent rhetorical pattern for showing how above-discharge draws out below-evil.

Confirming the editor's reading: "The waters were purified of the dark poison" is grammatically required as a passive construction, and the spiritual reading confirms the passive voice ("The falsities were purified").

The text consistently uses "pits" (¶1, ¶3, ¶7, ¶9) for the receptacles into which the vessels of evil are confined; "shut them in that pit of darkness" parallels the cosmological vocabulary throughout, and the spiritual reading's "region" corresponds to "pit" in the natural-plane register.

The spiritual reading explicitly confirms "and at" as the conjunction connecting the fire's descent to earth with the temporal clause "at that time again the fire that was shut in the earth below was drawn up"; this matches the chapter's pattern of sequential narration.

Confirming the editor's reading: "shut in the earth below" uses "shut in" as the standard collocation for confinement, matching ¶10's "shut them in that pit" and the spiritual reading's "confined in the natural states below."

Confirming the editor's reading: the active voice with "he" (the Father of Life) as subject is consistent with the chapter's style throughout ("he had established" in ¶3, "he poured" in ¶8–9), and the pluperfect indicates prior preparation of the outer underworld during the construction of the worlds.

The chapter consistently pairs "swept" with a subsequent action of expulsion — "swept outside and made them" (¶9), "swept them both out and shut them" (¶10), "swept it out and cast it" (¶11) — so this summary passage follows the same sweep-and-cast pattern to complete the removal action.
